newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief hopeful for ceasefire in Zaire conflict.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief hopeful for ceasefire in Zaire conflict.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Wednesday he was hopeful that the Zairean government and the rebels could set a date for a ceasefire during forthcoming talks in South Africa.

Answering queries from radio broadcasters in five continents, in a session carried live on the Internet, Annan said he expected both sides to agree on a date by the end of the week for both proper negotiations and a ceasefire.
He said he left an Africa summit in Lome, Togo, last week with the "understanding that the parties will accept a ceasefire and negotiations and that the date was to be announced later."
"I expect that the parties will agree to a date before the end of this week or not later than April 5," he said, adding that his special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun would then open the negotiations.
"So I would expect an announcement soon on a ceasefire and on commencement of talks," Annan said.
Some U.N. officials said there might be "proximity" or separate talks with mediators at the start in South Africa.
The Zairean government and the rebels have agreed to send negotiators to South Africa for the U.N.-led talks based on an agreement signed in Lome.

The two sides were to announce a ceasefire, which the Zairean government wants, when negotiations began. The rebels under Laurent Kabila want to talk about Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko giving up power.

"My sense is that once we get them to sit and we begin discussions and the ceasefire is declared we should do whatever we can to keep them at the table and get them to dissolve their differences political and discuss the future of Zaire," Annan said.
"I hope down the line there will be an election where all can participate and that the voice of the people will carry the day."
Kabila, head of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, was not expected to implement a ceasefire until his main military goals had been reached.
The rebels have seized about a third of the country and now have their sights set on Lubumbashi, capital of the mineral-rich Saba province.

Sahnoun, an Algerian, is also the special representative for Central Africa for the Organisation of African Unity. He told officials there would be no announcement for the talks, which may be held in Pretoria, until both parties arrive.
